user_prompt: I need to figure out who reports to whom across our company and understand the chain of command structure. Can you help me pull together the reporting relationships and organizational breakdown?

steps.step_name: I need to figure out who reports to whom across our company and understand the chain of command structure. Can you help me pull together the reporting relationships and organizational breakdown?

args.content:
LANDSCAPE INVENTORY:
- siemens.plm: PLM agents for engineering changes, BOM compliance, material provisioning
- corp.itsm: ITSM agents for IT infrastructure automation
- sap.odm: Canonical entity type taxonomy
- sap.s4: ERP core (procurement, BOM, asset lifecycle)
- sap.ariba: Procurement (vendor reconciliation, supplier compliance)
- sap.sf: HR agents (performance reviews, talent acquisition, compensation, skills matching) - NO org hierarchy/reporting structure
- workday.hcm: HR agents (performance reviews, compensation, safety) - NO org hierarchy/reporting structure
- emarsys.cx: Marketing/CX campaign orchestration
- sap.ehs: Safety/environmental compliance, incident management
- my.mes: Manufacturing Execution System (production quality, supplier compliance, engineering changes)

HR COMPENSATION CAPABILITIES (verified):
- sap.sf:agent:CompensationPolicyAutomationEngine: policy-driven salary adjustments
- workday.hcm:agent:CompensationAdjustmentAutomation: merit increases based on performance
- workday.hcm:agent:CompensationStructureAutomationEngine: compensation plan updates

ORDER & PRODUCTION SCHEDULING CAPABILITIES (verified):
- my.mes:agent:ProductionChangeOrchestrator: Orchestrates production changes
- my.mes:agent:ProductionQualityMonitor: Monitors ProductionOrders
- sap.s4:agent:OpportunityToOrderAutomationEngine: Creates orders from opportunities

NOTE: Landscape lacks organizational hierarchy/reporting structure capability. Both HR systems focus on transactional workflows (reviews, compensation, recruitment) not org design.
